chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Ibn Fazzal, from the one who mentioned it, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:

You are (living) in fixed terms and numbered days, and death comes unexpectedly. The one who cultivates goodness will harvest bliss, and the one who cultivates evil will harvest regret; and for every cultivator is what he cultivated. The slow-moving among you will not be preceded in his share, nor will the greedy one attain what was not decreed for him. Whoever is given good, Allah has given him; and whoever is protected from evil, Allah has protected him.

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'reaping what you sow' in Shia hadith regarding death and divine decree?
ai.summary: In the context of al-Kulayni’s *al-Kafi*, this narration underscores the transient nature of life (*ajal maqbulah*) and the inevitability of death, urging believers to maximize their limited days through conscious action. It integrates the concept of *al-hubb* (divine share/portion) with the principle of *man zara'a zara'a*, affirming that while outcomes are pre-ordained, individual effort determines the quality of one's harvest, reflecting the Shia balance between destiny and free will. The hadith concludes by attributing all blessings and protections directly to Allah, reinforcing divine generosity (*fadl*) and preservation (*hifz*) as the ultimate sources of good.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Ibn Fazzal, from the one who mentioned it, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘You are all (living) in a term which is being marked (allotted) and days which are numbered, and the death comes unexpectedly. The one who cultivates goodness would harvest (eternal) Bliss, but the one who cultivates evil would harvest regret; and for every farmer is what he farms; and the slow moving one from you will not be preceded by his share, nor would the greedy one comes across what is not Ordained for him. The one who does good, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> will Grant him good, but the one who saves (himself from) evil, So Allah<sup>azwj</sup> will Save evil for him’.
en.sarwar: 19. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn abu ‘Abd Allah from ibn Faddal from those whom has mentioned (in his book) from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “

You live in a period of time that is continuously reduced and in calculated days. Death comes suddenly. Whoever sows goodness will harvest what is very much sought after. Whoever sows evil will harvest regret. Every farmer finds what he has planted. The sustenance of the slow moving ones among you will not move ahead of him and the greedy will not achieve what is not assigned for him. Whoever does good, Allah grants him good and whoever safeguards against evil, Allah protects him.”
